snippet: # CDC social media silence during 2025 measles outbreak left void filled by news media, study suggests. As the United States faces its largest measles outbreak in three decades, one of the nation’s most storied public health voices has largely fallen silent on social media. A new exploratory analysis suggests that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) dramatically scaled back its social media posts during the first seven months of 2025, creating what researchers call a “health communication void.” That empty space was quickly filled by news media and, in some cases, less-credible voices. The study, published in *Vaccine*, examined measles and measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine-related posts from official CDC accounts on Facebook, Instagram, and X, alongside posts from major news outlets. What’s more, none of the CDC’s 2025 social media posts supported MMR vaccination, the most effective way to prevent measles infection.
